name: scene_entries
about: Ticket 16. At each history cut, one writer call gets only the Messages that leave, the names of the World cast and the Persona, and the last scene entry written before (read only, for the story time and the place). It answers one JSON object of scene entries. The tool adds them to a list that it never rewrites. The narrator sees the opening Narration word for word, then the scene entries, oldest first, in a <StoryMemory> block at the end of the user message before the history. A failed call (cut off, or not readable) adds nothing, and its Messages go to the next call.
list_head: Past scenes, oldest first. Each entry records what happened then. A state that an entry describes (a place, a mood, an object, a plan) may have changed since.
writer_system: You write the scene entries of the memory of an interactive story. The oldest Messages of the story leave the narrator's context now. You record them as scene entries, so that the narrator can continue the story without contradicting them. An entry is written once and never changes. Answer with one JSON object only.
writer_user:
The cast: {cast}. {persona} is the player character.

The last scene entry written before these Messages. Use it only for the story time and the place. Do not repeat it.

<PreviousEntry>
{previous_entry}
</PreviousEntry>

These are the story Messages #{first} to #{last}, which leave the narrator's context now. Messages marked {persona} are written by the player character. Messages marked Narration are written by the narrator.

<Messages>
{entries}
</Messages>

Split the Messages into scenes. A new scene starts when the place changes, when the story time jumps, or when the people who take part change. The first Messages can continue the scene of the previous entry, and the last scene can go on after #{last}. Write each part as its own entry.

For each scene, write one entry with these fields:
- "from", "to": the numbers of its first and its last Message. The entries cover #{first} to #{last} in order, with no gap and no overlap.
- "time": the story time, as the day of the story and the time of day, for example "Day 1, evening". Count the days from the start of the story. If the Messages do not say, carry on from the previous entry.
- "place": where the scene happens.
- "took_part": the names of the people who were in the scene, or spoke in it by phone. Use only names from the cast. A character merely mentioned, remembered, discussed, or addressed while absent is NOT a participant.
- "others": the people outside the cast who took part, by the name the story uses. An empty list if none.
- "what_happened": 60 to 150 words, in the past tense. Record what happened and its outcomes without treating past states as current. Keep the exact names, numbers, sums, dates and times, the objects and where they were left, the promises, plans and appointments with their times, the reasons that people gave, and who learned which fact (who was told, who overheard, who was not there).

Answer with this JSON object and nothing else:
{{"entries": [{{"from": 0, "to": 0, "time": "", "place": "", "took_part": [], "others": [], "what_happened": ""}}]}}
